$comment: SHARED CONTRACT for outbound public-projection PII suppression.
Arkova has TWO independent public, unauthenticated projections of the same
anchor rows, written in two languages:
1. SQL   — public.get_public_anchor(text) and its delegating sibling
`anon` and called straight from the browser over PostgREST by
the verify page, the embeddable widget, and the edge MCP tools.
They drifted, and the drift IS the defect: the CTDL path was hardened
(PR #1815) while the SQL path kept shipping learner names and raw
revocation reasons to anonymous callers. This file is the one place the
rule is written down, so neither implementation can be changed alone.
runs the vector corpus through the real anon-callable RPC).
TO CHANGE THE RULE: edit this file, then BOTH implementations, in ONE PR.
The tests fail otherwise — which is the entire point.
$ts_owner_note: ts_owner_module does not exist on main yet — it lands with PR #1815 (open,
out of draft). The contract test asserts its absence today and asserts full
parity the moment the file appears, so this arms itself with no follow-up
ticket. When #1815 merges, ts_owner_pending_pr becomes historical; leave it
as the record of why the self-arming branch exists.
DO NOT read this as 'the two implementations agree on main today'. They do
not. main's TS-side gate still lives in ts_pre_1815_module, and it is the
PRE-fix implementation that #1815 replaces. Measured divergences from this
contract, as of 2026-08-01:
- gates on DEGREE/CERTIFICATE only, AND requires a transcript keyword in
the free text; TRANSCRIPT is never gated by type. That is the bug #1815
fixes and the reason the SQL side could not simply copy it.
- no MAX_SCAN_CHARS; detectors run unbounded.
- 3 high-confidence families (email, SSN, phone), not 7.
- its SSN pattern makes separators OPTIONAL, so it fires on any bounded
9-digit run. The SQL side deliberately does not copy that: on a public
projection it would blank real fields containing an order number or a
numeric URL path segment.
The SQL detectors were verified vector-for-vector against #1815's guard, not
against ts_pre_1815_module. Parity with main becomes true when #1815 lands,
and the self-arming test starts enforcing it the same moment.
$academic_record_note: Records ABOUT AN IDENTIFIED LEARNER. These emit NO issuer- or
extraction-authored free text on either public projection.
CPE/CLE are deliberately EXCLUDED: practitioner records, not FERPA academic
records, and their descriptive title is the partner-facing value.
EVERY addition to this set silently replaces real credential titles with
$controlled_label_divergence: The CTDL serializer's academicRecordName() resolves a degree LEVEL from the
CTDL @type map ('Master Degree'). That map does not exist in the database,
so the SQL projection flattens DEGREE to 'Academic Degree'. TRANSCRIPT ->
'Academic Transcript' and CERTIFICATE -> 'Certificate' match the TS side
exactly. This divergence is DOCUMENTED, not silent — both labels are still
controlled vocabulary derived only from an enum, so neither can carry PII.
COPY SURFACE: these strings are USER-VISIBLE (the verify page renders
`filename` as the display title and embeds it in schema.org JSON-LD) but
they live in SQL, so `npm run lint:copy` cannot see them. If you widen this
map, check the new label against the CLAUDE.md §1.3 banned-terminology list
BY HAND — no linter covers this surface.
$ferpa_note: A THIRD education-type list lives in ferpa_module and deliberately DIFFERS:
it includes CLE. It drives the FERPA §99.33 re-disclosure NOTICE on the
verification API, not free-text suppression, and a continuing-legal-education
record is a practitioner record whose descriptive title is the partner-facing
value. Two lists with two purposes is fine. Two lists where nobody knows the
second exists is how this class of bug happens — so the contract test pins it,
and changing it is a decision rather than an accident.
$suppressed_vs_controlled: `filename` is the record's DISPLAY TITLE on the verify page and is embedded
in its schema.org JSON-LD, so it cannot be NULLed without breaking consumers
that assume a non-empty string — it takes a controlled label instead. It is
metadata.title and metadata.credential_title are OMITTED rather than given
the label. Emitting it there would leave the `metadata` object non-empty
after jsonb_strip_nulls, which flips the verify card out of its 'no metadata'
render mode into the key-value list — where neither key is hidden — and the
card would read 'Title: Academic Degree' and 'Credential Title: Academic
Degree' beneath a type banner that already says 'Academic Degree'. Omitting
preserves the existing render shape and states the label exactly once.
$url_note: Emitted URLs (proof_url, source_url, registry_url) go through a URL-specific
cleaner that DROPS on overflow instead of truncating. Truncating a URL
produces a valid-looking WRONG link that the frontend renders as a live
anchor — strictly worse than omitting the field. Query string and fragment
are stripped BEFORE the PII scan: structural, not heuristic, since a query
parameter is the carrier an identifier rides in on.
$learner_name_divergence: The CTDL serializer carries two capitalised-pair name patterns for
field-level suppression. The SQL projection deliberately does NOT implement
them. Measured, not assumed:
TRUE POSITIVES: zero. Run against this file's own leak_vectors, both
patterns return false for every single one — bare, all-caps, non-ASCII,
record-noun-first, apostrophe, hyphenated. `[A-Z][a-z]{1,}` cannot express
those shapes. Both implementations agree on this; it is the empirical
confirmation of PR #1815's own finding.
FALSE POSITIVES: abundant, because `for` is a bare preposition. 'Center
for Professional Development', 'Society for Human Resource Management',
'Institute for Supply Management', 'Ethics for Trial Lawyers', 'Credit for
Prior Learning', 'Revoked for Non Payment' — all dropped. The second
pattern takes ordinary titles the same way: 'Data Science degree',
'Project Management certificate'.
A detector with zero measured true positives and abundant measured false
positives has negative value, and the cost is higher here than on the CTDL
path: these fields are the verify page's PRIMARY DISPLAY (`filename` is the
record title and its schema.org `name`), not optional JSON-LD properties.
Learner names ARE covered on this path, structurally — an academic record
emits no issuer- or extraction-authored free text at all, which is
precision-independent and catches every shape above.
The false-positive strings are pinned in must_publish_vectors, so
reintroducing the patterns fails the suite rather than silently blanking
real credentials.
$detector_note: High-confidence detectors are FORMAT- or KEYWORD-anchored, run on every
credential type, and are the only ones precise enough to act on alone.
